trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to production, it failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also unhealthy in staging. I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, leaving regions on different versions (us-east v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west v2.3.1). A retry finished the rollback in all regions. Current state: v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west; healthy; error rate about 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error that stopped the rollout, and check why v2.3.1 reached production after failing in staging.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and it's healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open as INC-0001.

**Rollback**
- v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 had also failed in staging (as v2.3.1-rc).
- The first rollback stopped after us-east because of an error in the deployment system, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version again is safe, so I retried once and it finished in all regions.
- checkout-api is now on v2.3.0 in all three regions and healthy, with an error rate of about 0.2%.

**Incident INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api)**
- The request to create it timed out. Before retrying, I checked the incident list and found it had been created, so I didn't resend it. That avoided opening a duplicate and paging on-call twice.
- It describes what happened and the rollback, including the failed first attempt. It lists three follow-ups:
  - Find out why v2.3.1 failed.
  - Look into the error that stopped the first rollback.
  - Find out how v2.3.1 reached production after failing in staging.
